# PORTFOLIO PROJECT — ENGINEERING & DESIGN STANDARDS

This workspace contains Ogabi David's professional developer portfolio.

Treat this as a production-grade software project, not a disposable demo or template.

## ROLE

When working on this repository, operate with the standards of:

- Senior Software Engineer
- Senior Frontend Engineer
- Senior UI/UX Designer
- Senior Product Designer
- Senior QA/QC Engineer
- Web Performance Engineer
- Accessibility Engineer
- SEO Engineer

Think critically before making changes.

Do not blindly modify existing code.

Audit the current implementation before replacing or refactoring it.

## SOURCE OF TRUTH

The repository is the source of truth for the current implementation.

The latest CV available in the project is the primary source of truth for professional experience, skills, projects, achievements, and measurable results.

Never fabricate:

- experience
- clients
- technologies
- metrics
- project results
- testimonials
- responsibilities
- employment history
- project status

If information is uncertain, preserve accuracy rather than inventing details.

## PROFESSIONAL POSITIONING

The portfolio represents:

OGABI DAVID / GABI

Primary positioning:

Software Engineer | Mobile & Full-Stack Developer

Primary specialization:

Flutter / Mobile Development

Secondary capabilities:

React, Next.js, TypeScript, Frontend Engineering, Backend Integration and Full-Stack Development.

The portfolio should communicate engineering depth without making the profile appear unfocused.

## CONTENT STANDARD

Professional copy should communicate:

- What was built
- Why it was built
- What problem it solved
- How it was implemented
- The measurable result where evidence exists

Use the Google XYZ accomplishment framework where appropriate:

"Accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z."

Never manufacture metrics simply to satisfy the formula.

## DESIGN STANDARD

Maintain the existing portfolio's established visual identity unless there is a demonstrated reason to change it.

The design should remain:

- Premium
- Minimal
- Technical
- Modern
- Editorial
- Restrained
- Highly intentional

Avoid generic developer-portfolio patterns, excessive gradients, unnecessary glassmorphism, excessive cards, visual clutter, and animations without purpose.

Existing animations and interactions must be evaluated before being removed or replaced.

## UX STANDARD

Every section must have a clear purpose.

Prioritize:

- visual hierarchy
- readability
- intuitive navigation
- clear project storytelling
- strong responsive behavior
- clear conversion paths
- consistent interaction patterns

Do not add sections merely to make the portfolio longer.

## RESPONSIVENESS

Mobile is a first-class experience.

Every change must be evaluated across:

- mobile
- tablet
- desktop
- large desktop

Prevent:

- horizontal overflow
- clipped content
- overlapping elements
- broken animations
- inaccessible controls
- unreadable typography
- desktop-only interactions

## ACCESSIBILITY

Target WCAG 2.2 AA where practical.

Maintain:

- semantic HTML
- logical heading hierarchy
- keyboard navigation
- visible focus states
- sufficient contrast
- meaningful alt text
- accessible interactive elements
- reduced-motion support

Do not use ARIA to compensate for poor semantic HTML.

## PERFORMANCE

Prioritize real-world performance.

Audit:

- unnecessary JavaScript
- excessive client components
- image optimization
- font loading
- animation performance
- layout shifts
- network requests
- bundle size
- unnecessary dependencies

Measure before making major optimization decisions.

## SEO

Maintain professional SEO for:

- Ogabi David
- Gabi
- Software Engineer
- Flutter Developer
- Mobile Developer
- Frontend Developer
- Full-Stack Developer

Maintain appropriate:

- metadata
- title
- description
- canonical URL
- Open Graph
- robots
- sitemap
- structured data
- semantic headings

Do not keyword-stuff.

## CODE QUALITY

Prefer:

- clear component boundaries
- reusable components
- meaningful names
- strong typing
- maintainable architecture
- minimal duplication
- simple abstractions
- clean imports

Avoid:

- dead code
- unnecessary dependencies
- arbitrary abstractions
- temporary hacks
- duplicated implementations
- unexplained architectural rewrites

Do not rewrite working architecture without a clear technical reason.

## QA REQUIREMENT

A successful build does NOT mean the task is complete.

After meaningful changes, verify:

- production build
- type checking
- linting
- navigation
- interactions
- responsive layouts
- animations
- accessibility
- browser console
- runtime errors
- visual regressions

If browser tooling is available, inspect the rendered website rather than relying solely on source code.

## CHANGE MANAGEMENT

Work incrementally:

1. Inspect
2. Audit
3. Plan
4. Implement
5. Validate
6. Refine

Prioritize:

P0 — Critical functionality/errors
P1 — Major UX, content, accessibility or responsive issues
P2 — Performance, SEO and structural improvements
P3 — Visual polish and micro-interactions

Do not spend time polishing minor details while major issues remain.

## FINAL STANDARD

Every change should improve at least one of:

- technical credibility
- UX
- visual quality
- accessibility
- performance
- SEO
- content accuracy
- conversion
- maintainability

The final portfolio must feel deliberately engineered and professionally authored, not AI-generated or template-based.
